title: Getting Money Out of Your Pension Account Just Got Easier: Understanding NPS Partial Withdrawals
description: The Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA) has simplified rules for taking out some money from your NPS account. You can now make partial w.

faq.q: Who is eligible for a partial withdrawal from NPS?
faq.a: Any NPS subscriber who has completed at least three years in the scheme can apply for a partial withdrawal.

faq.q: What are the main reasons allowed for partial withdrawals?
faq.a: You can withdraw for children's higher education or marriage, buying/renovating a house, treatment of critical illnesses, or for establishing a new business/skill development.

faq.q: How much money can I take out?
faq.a: You can withdraw up to 25% of the contributions you have personally made to your NPS Tier-I account.

faq.q: Is there a limit to how many times I can make a partial withdrawal?
faq.a: Yes, you can make a maximum of three partial withdrawals during the entire tenure of your NPS subscription.

faq.q: How quickly can I get the money after applying?
faq.a: With the simplified online process and self-declaration, funds are typically credited to your bank account within a few working days.
